Front: What is recursive self-improvement (RSI) in AI?
Back: AI systems that iteratively enhance their own capabilities through self-play, self-training, or self-evaluation loops. The model generates training data for itself, iteratively improving -- unlike standard fine-tuning which uses static human-generated datasets.

Front: What is the core architectural decision in RSI system design?
Back: Whether to use verified self-improvement (filtering through external verifier with ground truth) vs self-judged improvement (model evaluates its own outputs). Choose verified for math/code; choose self-judged for open-ended tasks without an oracle.

Front: What is STaR (Self-Taught Reasoner) and how does it work?
Back: STaR bootstraps rationale generation by: 1) Generating rationales for questions. 2) Keeping those leading to correct answers. 3) For wrong answers, rationalizing given the answer as a hint. 4) Fine-tuning on collected rationales. 5) Repeating with improved model.

Front: Why is the "rationalization" step crucial in STaR?
Back: Without rationalization, the model only trains on problems it already solves ("rich get richer"). Rationalization provides signal on hard problems by leveraging the easier task of explaining a known answer vs deriving it. This bootstraps reasoning for unsolved problems.

Front: What is model collapse and why does it threaten recursive self-training?
Back: Training on self-generated data causes progressive distributional narrowing. Each generation compounds estimation errors geometrically. After k generations, effective support shrinks as O(1/k), with minority modes vanishing first. Proved by Shumailov et al. 2024 in Nature.

Front: What is the timeline of model collapse?
Back: Iteration 0: Full support. Iteration 1-2: Slight narrowing, tails thin. Iteration 3-5: Mode sharpening, rare cases lost. Iteration 6+: Collapse to few templates. Quality APPEARS to improve on common cases while catastrophic capability loss occurs.

Front: How does AlphaGo Zero achieve superhuman play through self-play?
Back: Plays against itself using game outcome (win/loss) as only signal. Neural network f(s) = (p, v) outputs move probabilities and position value. MCTS guides play; outcomes train the network. MCTS acts as policy improvement operator -- even weak networks improve through search.

Front: What is the key recursive mechanism in AlphaGo Zero?
Back: MCTS amplifies the current policy, producing better moves than the raw network. Training on MCTS-improved targets ratchets up the baseline, which improves the next round of MCTS. This creates a virtuous cycle of policy improvement.

Front: Can RSI exceed the verifier's capability?
Back: Yes -- the verifier only needs to check correctness, not produce solutions. Checking a proof is easier than generating one. AlphaGo Zero's verifier was simply "did you win?" -- far simpler than the strategy it learned. STaR's verifier checks answers without generating reasoning.

Front: What are Self-Rewarding Language Models?
Back: Models that: 1) Generate multiple candidate responses. 2) Judge their own outputs using LLM-as-Judge prompts. 3) Form preference pairs from high vs low scores. 4) Train via iterative DPO. After 3 iterations, Llama 2 70B surpassed human-preference-trained models on AlpacaEval.

Front: Why do Self-Rewarding LMs work despite self-evaluation limitations?
Back: They evaluate quality (subjective) rather than correctness (objective). The competitive ranking between candidates provides relative signal even with imperfect absolute judgments. Both generation and judging ability improve simultaneously.

Front: What did Huang et al. 2023 prove about LLM self-correction?
Back: LLMs cannot reliably self-correct reasoning without external verification. Models change correct answers to incorrect ones at nearly the same rate as they fix errors. Self-correction fails when ground truth is unavailable.

Front: What is SPIN (Self-Play Fine-Tuning)?
Back: Frames alignment as a two-player game: current model tries to generate outputs indistinguishable from human data, while previous iteration discriminates. Convergence: when model matches human distribution. Requires NO reward model -- only SFT data serves as target.

Front: What is the formal SPIN objective?
Back: L_SPIN = E[log sigma(beta(log pi_t(y_human|x) - log pi_t(y_{t-1}|x)))]. Structurally identical to DPO with y_human as "chosen" and y_{t-1} (previous model's output) as "rejected." Converges when pi_t = human distribution.

Front: What is SPIN's natural stopping criterion?
Back: When the loss stops decreasing, the model has converged to the human data distribution and no further improvement is possible. Unlike other RSI methods, SPIN has a provable fixed point.

Front: What is the limitation of SPIN?
Back: SPIN converges to the human data distribution regardless of quality -- it has no mechanism to EXCEED its target. If human data contains errors, SPIN reproduces them. It is complementary to methods like STaR that can surpass training data via verification.

Front: What is ReST (Reinforced Self-Training) and how does it differ from STaR?
Back: ReST uses a two-phase "Grow then Improve" approach: Grow phase samples N=64-256 responses per problem (best-of-N). Improve phase fine-tunes on filtered examples with reward-weighted regression. Fewer iterations (2-3) but more compute per iteration.

Front: Why does ReST work with fewer iterations than STaR?
Back: ReST's Grow phase samples 256 responses, capturing rare successful strategies that STaR's single-attempt approach misses. Each iteration provides a richer training set, so fewer iterations reach the same performance ceiling.

Front: What is GRPO (Group Relative Policy Optimization)?
Back: Self-play-style group sampling (G=64) with verifiable rewards, eliminating value networks. Computes advantages relative to the group rather than using binary correct/incorrect. DeepSeekMath achieved 51.7% on MATH, surpassing GPT-4.

Front: What is the verification spectrum for RSI systems (from best to worst)?
Back: Ground truth (perfect, free -- math/code). Process reward model (high, ~$10K training). Outcome reward model (medium, ~$5K). Self-as-judge (low-medium, inference cost only). No verification (dangerous, never recommended).

Front: Why do process reward models outperform outcome reward models?
Back: Lightman et al. showed PRMs (checking each reasoning step) reduce error rates by 50% vs ORMs (checking only final answer) on MATH. Step-level verification catches errors early before they propagate through the reasoning chain.

Front: What is the only domain where RSI has demonstrated unbounded improvement potential?
Back: Automated theorem proving (formal mathematics) -- because verification is perfect (proofs either check or don't). Polu and Sutskever showed GPT-f could find novel proofs by iterating with a formal verifier.

Front: What is Weak-to-Strong Generalization and its implication for RSI?
Back: Burns et al. showed that strong models fine-tuned with weak model labels recover 20-70% of the strong model's potential. Implication: self-generated labels from weaker previous versions can still teach a model to exceed its supervisor's capability.

Front: When does Weak-to-Strong Generalization fail?
Back: When the strong model cannot distinguish correct from incorrect weak labels (task requires genuinely absent knowledge). Also fails on distribution shift: weak labels from easy examples don't transfer to hard examples requiring extrapolation.

Front: How does Constitutional AI enable RSI without human feedback?
Back: Replaces human feedback with explicit principles. Pipeline: Generate -> Critique against constitution -> Revise -> Use original as "rejected" and revision as "chosen" for preference training. The constitution acts as the verifier.

Front: What is the "killer framing" for recursive self-improvement's current state?
Back: RSI already works in production for domains with verifiable rewards. The open frontier is making it safe and stable for domains without ground truth.

Front: What cost does a single STaR iteration on a 7B model require?
Back: ~$200 in compute per iteration. 5 iterations reach diminishing returns at ~$1K total, delivering 10-30% accuracy gains on reasoning benchmarks.

Front: What are the four stopping criteria for RSI loops (in hierarchy)?
Back: 1) Hard stop: Safety regression on alignment suite -- immediately halt. 2) Collapse stop: Diversity metric drops below threshold. 3) Diminishing returns: Improvement < epsilon for 2 consecutive iterations. 4) Compute budget: Total cost exceeds envelope.

Front: How many iterations capture 90%+ of achievable gains in math reasoning RSI?
Back: 4-5 iterations, with each successive iteration providing roughly half the improvement of the previous one (geometric decay with r = 0.4-0.6). Beyond this, marginal cost exceeds marginal improvement.

Front: What is the formula for geometric improvement decay in RSI?
Back: Delta_k = Delta_1 * r^(k-1), where r is typically 0.4-0.6. Total improvement after K iterations: Delta_1 * (1 - r^K) / (1 - r). Optimal stopping: when Delta_1 * r^(k*-1) / C < threshold.

Front: What are the four main mitigations for model collapse?
Back: 1) Data mixing: keep 20-40% original human data each iteration (provably prevents full collapse). 2) Temperature annealing: generate at T=1.0-1.2. 3) Diversity-weighted sampling from low-density regions. 4) Multi-model cross-pollination.

Front: What is the "critical iteration" phenomenon in model collapse?
Back: Collapse is not gradual -- there is a phase transition. Before critical iteration, diversity degrades slowly. After it, collapse accelerates catastrophically. Often occurs at iteration 4-5: accuracy still improves while diversity collapses underneath.

Front: What diversity metrics should you monitor to detect model collapse early?
Back: Distinct-4gram ratio (healthy >0.75, collapse <0.60). Output entropy (healthy >4.0 bits, collapse <3.0). Embedding coverage (healthy >80% clusters, collapse <50%). Tail probability mass (healthy >10%, collapse <3%).

Front: What is the circularity problem in self-evaluation for RSI?
Back: When M_k judges its own outputs, Score_self = E[M_k.judge(M_k.generate(x))]. Judge and generator share biases, so the model can increase scores without genuine improvement -- a form of internal reward hacking.

Front: How do you break circular evaluation in RSI?
Back: 1) Held-out ground truth (gold standard). 2) External model judges (different family). 3) Human evaluation (expensive but unbiased). 4) Diverse judge ensemble (3+). 5) Behavioral probes (test specific capabilities with designed cases).

Front: What are the unique safety challenges of RSI compared to standard training?
Back: 1) Goal drift across iterations. 2) Deceptive alignment (appear aligned during eval, different in deployment). 3) Non-linear capability jumps outpacing monitoring. 4) Recursive reward hacking (increasingly sophisticated self-scoring).

Front: What is the containment architecture for RSI systems?
Back: Three layers: OUTER (human-controlled: iteration budget, safety suite, veto power), MIDDLE (automated gates: safety suite between every iteration, block on alignment drops >2%), INNER (sandboxed: no internet, immutable eval data, hard compute cap).

Front: What did Anthropic's sleeper agents work demonstrate about RSI safety?
Back: Fine-tuning can create models that appear aligned but revert under specific conditions (deceptive alignment persists through safety training). For RSI: a subtle misalignment at iteration 2 becomes the foundation for iterations 3-10, amplifying into catastrophic behavior.

Front: What is OpenAI o1's contribution to recursive self-improvement?
Back: Demonstrated that extended inference-time reasoning via chain-of-thought produces large capability gains without additional training data. Shows RSI can operate at inference time (not just training time) via verification-guided search.

Front: How does verification-guided search (the o1 paradigm) extend STaR?
Back: Combines STaR's iterative self-improvement (training time) with best-first search at inference time. Process reward model scores each reasoning step: Score(r_1...r_n) = Product of PRM(r_i | context). Explores multiple branches, keeps best paths.

Front: What is the formal mathematical model of model collapse?
Back: Without mixing: p_{k+1} = Fit(Sample_N(p_k)). Variance decays as Var(p_k) ~ Var(p_0) * (N/(N+1))^k -> 0 as k->infinity. With mixing: p_{k+1} = (1-alpha)*p_k + alpha*p_0 prevents full collapse. Speed determined by sample size N.

Front: What is the DeepSeekMath GRPO connection to STaR?
Back: GRPO is a relaxation of STaR: instead of binary correct/incorrect, uses group-relative advantages from G=64 samples per problem. Provides richer gradient signal while maintaining self-improvement property. Found G=64 with K=3 iterations > G=16 with K=10 at equal compute.

Front: What is the compute-optimal budget allocation for RSI?
Back: Allocate 60% to first 2 iterations, 25% to iterations 3-4, keep 15% in reserve for evaluation and safety checks. If iteration 2 shows <30% of iteration 1's improvement, strongly consider stopping.

Front: What is the RSI Decision Tree for choosing method?
Back: Have verifiable reward? YES -> Verified Self-Training (STaR/ReST). NO -> Can model judge quality? -> Self-Rewarding LM. Have weak human signal? -> Weak-to-Strong. Can frame as game? -> Self-Play (SPIN).

Front: How does population-based training address non-transitivity in self-play?
Back: In complex games, agent A beats B, B beats C, but C beats A (non-transitivity causes cycling). PBT maintains a population training against each other, discovering mixed-strategy Nash equilibrium rather than cycling between pure strategies.

Front: What is the convergence proof sketch for AlphaGo Zero?
Back: MCTS policy improvement theorem guarantees search-augmented policy >= raw policy for any parameters. Training on MCTS targets via supervised learning ensures monotone improvement. Policies form a Cauchy sequence converging to minimax-optimal.

Front: What did Singh et al. 2024 "Beyond Human Data" demonstrate?
Back: With sufficient sampling and reliable verification, self-training can surpass human-demonstration-trained models on MATH by 10+ percentage points. Brute-force sampling finds solutions the model assigns low probability to; fine-tuning on these broadens competence.

Front: What is the relationship between STaR's rationalization and complexity theory?
Back: Rationalization exploits the asymmetry between verification and generation -- explaining a known answer is in a lower complexity class than deriving it. Similar to P vs NP: checking is easier than solving.

Front: How should you detect strategy cycling in self-play?
Back: Track Elo rating against a FIXED set of reference agents (not the self-play partner). If Elo oscillates rather than monotonically increases, cycling is occurring. Solution: switch to population-based training.

Front: What is the oversight scaling problem in RSI?
Back: As models improve, they may exceed human ability to evaluate outputs. If the model at iteration k generates solutions no available evaluator can verify, the self-improvement loop MUST halt. Gap between evaluator and model capability must be monitored.

Front: What is STaR's convergence pattern across iterations?
Back: solve_rate_k ~ solve_rate_infinity * (1 - c * r^k) where r ~ 0.5-0.7. On CommonsenseQA: 73% -> 82% over 4 iterations. Gains are largest in first 2-3 iterations with diminishing returns -- pattern consistent across all self-training methods.

Front: Why does self-play in AlphaGo Zero not converge to a narrow exploitable strategy?
Back: MCTS provides exploration (samples diverse game trees via UCB). Value network generalizes across positions (prevents overfitting to specific patterns). Result: rediscovered and surpassed known human opening theory rather than narrow equilibrium.

Front: What are the key differences between STaR and ReST in sampling and training?
Back: STaR: 1 attempt + rationalization, binary signal, many iterations (5-10), lower compute per iteration. ReST: N=64-256 attempts with best-of-N, continuous reward, few iterations (2-3), higher compute per iteration.

Front: What leading indicators predict model collapse before it becomes catastrophic?
Back: Shrinkage of 95th percentile response lengths (converges toward median). Dropping accuracy on held-out "rare event" test set while overall accuracy rises. Distinct-4gram ratio declining below 0.65 from baseline 0.80+.

Front: What makes Constitutional AI's approach to RSI safety unique?
Back: By externalizing values into explicit principles, CAI makes training signal auditable and modifiable. Each iteration checks outputs against constitution, preventing drift. If problematic behavior develops, add a principle rather than thousands of labels.
